final_candidates.decision_summary: W17 is a large aromatic residue in the N-terminal core (within the conserved YWY motif); replacing it with glycine removes aromatic/hydrophobic packing and adds backbone flexibility, strongly favoring unfolding.
L11 sits in the hydrophobic N-terminal segment; introducing a buried negative charge should severely destabilize core packing and disrupt folding.
F40 is a bulky hydrophobe in the central I/V-rich cluster; hydrophobic-to-charge substitution at this central position is expected to be highly destabilizing to the fold.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are verified, well-differentiated in mechanism, and further self-iteration offers no expected improvement.

history.rationale: W17 sits in the conserved YWY aromatic motif; removing the bulky tryptophan for glycine should collapse local hydrophobic packing and increase backbone flexibility, disrupting the SH3-like fold core.
W17 is a conserved aromatic core residue; replacing it with glycine should maximally remove hydrophobic/aromatic packing and increase local flexibility.
L11 is a buried hydrophobic residue in the N-terminal region; introducing a charged aspartate into the hydrophobic core is strongly destabilizing.
Introducing aspartate at buried hydrophobic L11 should strongly disrupt core packing and solubility-compatible folding.
F40 is likely a core-packing aromatic; a phenylalanine-to-aspartate change places an uncompensated negative charge in the hydrophobic interior.
F40 is a bulky hydrophobic residue in the central region; charge substitution is likely to be highly destabilizing.
Y16 is part of the conserved YWY motif essential for PsaE structure/PsaC interaction; truncating it to alanine removes key aromatic packing.
Y16A removes an aromatic interaction but alanine is less destabilizing than glycine or buried charge, so it is downgraded.
I33 is a buried hydrophobic residue adjacent to the DKS loop; an Asp substitution should disrupt core packing and solvation balance.
I33D places a charged residue in a hydrophobic cluster and is reranked upward as a core-disrupting candidate comparable to F40D.
P35 likely enforces a critical turn conformation; alanine removes this conformational constraint and may misfold the loop region.
Removing P35 may perturb local geometry, but alanine can be tolerated and does not guarantee global knockout.

rejection.reason: Removing P35 may perturb local geometry, but alanine can be tolerated and does not guarantee global knockout.

history.rationale: V38 is a hydrophobic core residue; introducing a charged residue into the beta-sheet interior should be destabilizing.
V38D remains a plausible hydrophobic-to-charge disruption but may be less central than residues 11, 17, 33, and 40.
F60 is an aromatic residue likely contributing to C-terminal packing; replacement with aspartate introduces an unsatisfied charge.
F60D could disrupt a later hydrophobic/contact region, but its C-terminal location may be less folding-critical than the N/Mid core.
L55 is hydrophobic and likely buried near the glycine-rich region; a charged substitution should destabilize local packing.
Rejected to prioritize higher-confidence core substitutions; L55 appears less central and has weaker expected folding disruption.

rejection.reason: Rejected to prioritize higher-confidence core substitutions; L55 appears less central and has weaker expected folding disruption.

history.rationale: G54 in the GG motif may require glycine-only backbone geometry; alanine could introduce steric strain, though effect size is uncertain.
G54A is too conservative for the stated knockout objective and is unlikely to strongly destabilize folding.

rejection.reason: G54A is too conservative for the stated knockout objective and is unlikely to strongly destabilize folding.
